elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: § 10.4 is retained unchanged: "Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I". Ownership stays with Vendor; the redline deliberately does not reverse it.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere; the insertion is a licence grant ("M&I grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license..."), not an assignment, and § 10.4's Vendor-ownership sentence survives.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: § 10.4 ("All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property") and § 17.2 (Customer "has no rights in any software, systems, documentation...provided by M&I", now subject only to the new licence) leave Vendor's pre-existing IP with Vendor.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The new grant is limited to "the Developed Software"; it does not address M&I pre-existing IP embedded in that Developed Software, and § 17.2 still confines Customer's rights in M&I software/systems to "use of the same during the Term". No perpetual embedded-IP licence results.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same defect: "irrevocable" attaches only to the Developed Software licence; embedded M&I pre-existing IP remains governed by the Term-limited § 17.2 acknowledgement.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "Royalty-free" appears only in the Developed Software grant; there is no royalty-free licence expressed for M&I IP embedded in deliverables.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: § 17.1 retained: "Customer shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and other Confidential Information", with a broad "Customer Data" definition covering all data submitted to or received by M&I for Customer.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: No Vendor licence to exploit Customer Data is granted anywhere; § 17.4 restricts Vendor to holding Customer's Confidential Information in confidence and not using it "other than for the purposes contemplated by this Agreement", with need-to-know distribution only. Note the wording is "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" rather than "solely to provide the Services" — slightly broader, but no distribution, resale or independent-exploitation right survives (the § 17.1 regulator-examination carve-out is not Vendor exploitation).

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in §§ 10.4, 17.1–17.4 or the insertion; ownership is allocated wholly to one party in each case.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Already met and left intact: "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant: "M&I grants Customer a perpetual...license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software"; "Developed Software" is defined in § 10.4 as any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in performing the Services, i.e. the deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Grant reads "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears expressly in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" appears expressly in the inserted grant; no further payment mechanic is imposed on the licence (the § 10.4 refund/credit machinery is untouched and operates in Customer's favour).

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business"; § 17.2's Term-only limitation is conformed by "Except as provided in Section 10.5", so no contradictory retained sentence on scope.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "sublicense" is expressly included in the inserted grant, for Customer's business.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: § 17.1 keeps Customer as sole and exclusive owner and § 17.4 bars Vendor use or disclosure "other than for the purposes contemplated by this Agreement"; no resale, distribution or independent-exploitation right over Customer Data exists (§ 10.4's resale right is confined to Developed Software, not Customer Data).

reasons: Fallback is position-complete on substance: the inserted grant supplies perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense rights in the Developed Software for Customer's business, Vendor's ownership of programs and know-how is left intact, and Customer Data protection (§§ 17.1, 17.4) already satisfies the data element.

Preferred is correctly not claimed: § 10.4's Vendor-ownership sentence survives, there is no assignment to Customer, and no perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence is expressed for M&I pre-existing IP embedded in deliverables (§ 17.2 still limits M&I-system rights to the Term).

Minimality holds: only two operations — one concise insertion of the licence and a five-word conforming carve-out in § 17.2. No survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no extra remedies or procedures, and no favourable existing language (including the § 10.4 refund/credit mechanic and the confidentiality obligations) was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent defect to repair: § 17.2 now reads "Except as provided in Section 10.5", but the inserted clause is rendered as an unnumbered paragraph headed "License to Developed Software." while every surrounding provision carries its number. As rendered this is a dangling cross-reference. Fix by numbering the insertion "10.5 License to Developed Software." (or by pointing § 17.2 at the actual clause number).

Optional wording tightening, not a blocker: consider "solely to provide the Services" in place of reliance on § 17.4's broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" if the data limit is ever renegotiated; the current language is acceptable because no Vendor exploitation right over Customer Data exists.
